chapter_title: Concerning the Seven Works of the Living Spirit
chapter_note: The chapter is dominated by a compact, enumerated cosmological teaching: the Living Spirit’s “seven works” (plus an added eschatological work) described in impersonal mythic/architectonic terms (rescuing First Man, constructing zone/ships, appointing powers, etc.). Only the opening dialogue attribution (“Once again the enlightener speaks”) and the final beatitude read as later framing/devotional material rather than the older systematic substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit has done seven [wo]rks with his strength.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "[Once] again the enlightener speaks:" (late hagiographic/compilation voice marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening formula with the speaker label “the enlightener” is a classic Kephalaia frame layer; the remaining sentence begins the old enumerative teaching topic.

paragraphs.core_text: [The fi]rst: He brought the First Man up from the contest, the way a pearl is [brought] up from the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Enumerated work within the cosmic drama (Living Spirit/First Man), using impersonal correspondential simile (pearl/sea) without institutional or NT citation markers.

paragraphs.core_text: [The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified [h]im in every body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the numbered mythic sequence; “crucified…in every body” functions here as internal cosmological language (binding a cosmic rebel in bodies), with no Gospel-citation vector.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: He [tr]ampled, piled up, and pierced the essences of death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmic action verbs in a numbered list; no audience address or institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: [The f]ourth: He constructed the ships of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure cosmological architecture (“ships of light”), matching the old teaching register.

paragraphs.core_text: The fi[f]th: He evoked his five sons, and distributed them about. They [took] possession of the zone, they bore up under all the universe's weight. Also, he evoked three living words. He set [them] upon the th[re]e vessels, another one upon the giant. [Again, he evoked the] summons, that it might be mixed with the five shining men.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Strong core markers: systematic numeration plus five-/three-fold structuring (five sons; three living words; three vessels), cosmic engineering (zone/universe weight), and internal process language (“summons…mixed”).

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.86⟩ The sixth: When he had constructed the zone he aro[se] and s[e]nt forth a multitude of powers and many [angel]s; so that they would bound the circuit of the z[o]ne on every si[de], un[t]il he finished [co]nstructing the works. And at the end [of] all the [wor]ks he to[ok s]ome of them into his storehouses, and he appointed others at the watch-posts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal logistical/cosmic-administrative description (zone circuit, storehouses, watch-posts) that stays within the universe’s architecture; no church/pastoral targets.

paragraphs.core_text: The [sev]enth: A[t the] time when the Ambass[ador dis]pl[aye]d his glorious imag[e], the L[iving] Spirit [established] many [go]ds and angels. They [ ... ] Th[ey to]ok hold of it, that the entire building [ ... ] not [ ... / ... ] one another against [the] light, which he had [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Still within the cosmic system (Ambassador, Living Spirit, gods/angels, safeguarding the building against assault on the light). Lacunae prevent finer segmentation but no clear late institutional/NT signals appear.

paragraphs.core_text: Also another gr[ea]t and glorious work he will enact at the e[nd] is [the] Last [Statue], which he will bring up to the aeons of [light]; and he [ ... ] in, and [he ta]kes hold, and he smites [ ... ], and [he] builds, and he [ ... ], and he [ ... t]hem.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological-cosmic closure motif (“Last Statue,” “aeons of light”) remains internal to Manichaean cosmology; no ecclesial application or Gospel citation formula.

Beatitude-style devotional closure (“Blessed is he…”) shifts from impersonal exposition to pious valuation/reward language; functions as a later framing/doxological ending rather than the enumerative substrate.
